avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Induces P-glycoprotein, increasing digoxin elimination and reducing serum levels below therapeutic range
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; use alternative antidepressant if needed

avoid_supplements.name: Ginseng
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May increase digoxin levels and cardiac effects; increases inotropic activity leading to arrhythmia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; monitor heart rate and rhythm if unavoidable

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Causes hypokalemia and sodium retention, increasing digoxin toxicity risk and arrhythmias
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; use alternative if needed; monitor potassium levels closely

avoid_supplements.name: Hawthorn
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates inotropic and arrhythmogenic effects of digoxin; additive cardiac activity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid use; consult cardiologist before use as supplement

avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Increases digoxin-induced arrhythmias by enhancing cardiac contractility and automaticity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose supplementation; use dietary sources only; maintain normal serum calcium

caution_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity risk; supplementation helps maintain therapeutic window
caution_supplements.action: May be beneficial; coordinate with prescriber and monitor serum potassium and digoxin levels

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Hypomagnesemia increases digoxin toxicity; supplementation may reduce arrhythmia risk
caution_supplements.action: May be appropriate; monitor magnesium and digoxin levels; doses should be moderate

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: May alter gut flora metabolism affecting digoxin absorption and enterohepatic recirculation
caution_supplements.action: Monitor digoxin levels if initiating probiotics; generally safe but individualize monitoring

avoid_foods.name: High-fiber foods (excessive intake)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Excessive fiber binds digoxin in GI tract, reducing absorption and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_foods.action: Maintain consistent (not excessive) fiber intake; separate timing of digoxin and high-fiber meals if possible

caution_foods.name: Potassium-rich foods (spinach, bananas, sweet potatoes)
caution_foods.mechanism: Hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity; dietary potassium helps maintain normal levels
caution_foods.action: Encourage moderate intake; coordinate with prescriber regarding diuretic use and potassium status

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: May inhibit P-glycoprotein, potentially increasing digoxin levels, though clinical significance is variable
caution_foods.action: Consistent intake acceptable; avoid sudden changes; monitor for toxicity signs if consumption increases

monitoring_notes: Digoxin has a narrow therapeutic window (0.5-2 ng/mL); serum level monitoring is essential, especially when supplements or significant dietary changes are introduced. Monitor for signs of toxicity (nausea, visual disturbances, arrhythmias) and maintain consistent potassium and magnesium levels.
